markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

Three starting-point insights guide this early-stage proposal. First, padding errors of 1.5769–1.9719 exceed the 1e-5 tolerance in every category. Context-removal results therefore cannot yet justify stronger recency weighting. Second, Movies and Electronics have sampled negative-win rates of 6.25% and 5.90%. These motivate ranking-loss experiments, but do not establish validation weaknesses. Third, users report both stale-interest emphasis and broad matches crowding out precise choices. Recency weighting and competitive-negative training address these distinct hypotheses; neither establishes equipment compatibility.

Three related-work insights constrain implementation. PyTorch GRUs update state even for zero inputs. Packing chronological nonpadding tokens removes those updates [1]. BPR-max concentrates training on competitive negatives through a probability mixture. Its score penalty is a separate experimental axis [2]. Temporal recurrent models support investigating time-dependent interests. Their results do not establish benefits here, and repeat-item prediction differs from ranking unseen items [3].

### Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Atomic proposal | O/F/U/M/D scores |
|---|---|---|
| Encoding correctness | Compact, pack, and scatter GRU outputs | 2/8/5/10/4 |
| Ranking discrimination | BPR-max with 16 uniform negatives | 3/7/7/8/4 |
| Target relevance | Absolute-event-recency target weights | 4/7/8/5/3 |

Scores denote originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. For encoding, the respective positives are established novelty scope, reusable correctness, stable histories, direct padding repair, and a standard API; negatives are little novelty, no guaranteed accuracy gain, indirect user impact, unresolved margins, and scatter bookkeeping. For BPR-max: positives are a focused adaptation, reusable objective, precise competition, weak-margin targeting, and a compact loss; negatives are an established method, dataset dependence, false negatives, training-only evidence, and sampling cost. For recency: positives are absolute-time specificity, temporal relevance, current-interest emphasis, testable weighting, and simple arithmetic; negatives are established decay, stale timestamps, possible loss of durable interests, confounded current evidence, and sampler metadata changes.

### Selected experiment

Select **padding-invariant GRU4Rec with separately tested BPR-max and absolute-event-recency weighting**. At 20% progress, correctness and controlled changes offer the clearest next step. It explicitly targets older interests displacing recent behavior and broad alternatives displacing closer matches; these remain hypotheses. Padding failure is its directly measured model-facing target.

```
compact nonzero inputs chronologically; pack through supplied GRU
scatter valid outputs to original positions
score positive and 16 distinct eligible uniform negatives
loss_t = -log(sum softmax(s_neg)*sigmoid(s_pos-s_neg))
w_t = 0.5 + 0.5*exp(-(latest_train_time-target_time)/tau)
optimize sum(w_t*loss_t)/sum(w_t)
```

First verify padding invariance, then compare baseline loss versus BPR-max with matched negatives, then enable weighting. Fix tau from training timestamps; keep score regularization disabled initially. Preserve all four categories, seeds, limits, diagnostic interfaces, and matching predictor code. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10, with exactly one checkpoint per category.

idea.description: Make the supplied GRU4Rec encoding invariant to left padding, then independently test BPR-max and bounded absolute-event-recency target weighting. Retain exactly one independently trained GRU model per category.
idea.motivation: All four supplied padding diagnostics fail, so encoding correctness precedes interpreting recency interventions. Competitive-negative training targets broad alternatives crowding out precise matches; timestamp weighting targets older or occasional interests displacing recent behavior. These are testable mechanisms, not demonstrated user or validation improvements.
idea.implementation_notes: Compact each sequence's nonzero tokens in chronological order before packing; never pack the original left-padded array directly. Unpack and scatter valid timestep outputs back to B x L for log2feats. Handle empty sequences with zero features; use the maximum nonpadding index for final readout. Preserve the supplied GRU architecture otherwise, item_emb, predict_score, family-specific sample_batch, ModelView, DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use the same encoding in training, diagnostics and the embedded predictor writer. Sample 16 distinct uniform negatives excluding padding, the target and observed training positives; use all eligible items if fewer exist. Implement BPR-max stably using log_softmax and logsigmoid followed by logsumexp. Initially disable its separate negative-score penalty. Compute recency from the original target timestamp and that user's latest training timestamp, never from window position or validation/test interactions; use tau equal to the median positive training-history span in the category, with weights of one when usable timestamps are unavailable. Retain the diagnostic loader's four-element tuple and obtain timestamp weights through a training-only side channel. Run sequential controlled comparisons: padding-corrected baseline, matched-pool BPR-max, then recency weighting. These are separate trials, never fused predictors. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, and the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], with artifacts beneath the trial directory. Select by the host's pinned macro validation HR@10. Verify padding invariance in eval mode for valid features and scores, including mixed-length batches. Report measured diagnostics with their definitions; do not infer compatibility, diversity or held-out performance from training margins.
idea.pseudocode:
For each required category:
    Initialize the supplied corrected GRU4Rec with seed 42
    Encode(sequence):
        Collect chronological nonzero tokens for each nonempty row
        Pack compacted rows and run the existing unidirectional GRU
        Unpack and scatter valid outputs to original sequence positions
        Return aligned features, with zeros at padding and empty rows
    For each training batch within fixed limits:
        features = Encode(sequence)
        Select valid input/positive positions
        Sample up to 16 distinct eligible uniform negatives per position
        positive_score = predict_score(features, positive)
        negative_scores = predict_score(features, negative_pool)
        log_mix = log_softmax(negative_scores, dim=-1)
        loss = -logsumexp(log_mix + logsigmoid(positive_score[..., None] - negative_scores), dim=-1)
        If recency weighting is enabled:
            age = latest_user_training_timestamp - original_target_timestamp
            weight = 0.5 + 0.5 * exp(-age / tau)
        Else: weight = 1
        Optimize sum(weight * loss) / sum(weight)
    Save one selected checkpoint and architecture configuration
Generate working/predict.py with identical encoding and four-category routing
Run unchanged host validation; retain one model per category without averaging

originality.positive: Separates padding correctness, competitive-negative ranking and absolute target recency in a controlled GRU4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: Packing, BPR-max and temporal decay are established techniques; the combination is an incremental research hypothesis.

future_potential.positive: Establishes interpretable tests of current-interest supervision after removing a directly observed encoding confound.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may vary across categories, and timestamp recency does not encode functional compatibility or satisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses standard PyTorch packing and a compact ranking loss without additional independently trained components.
code_difficulty.negative: Aligned feature scattering, timestamp bookkeeping, negative exclusions and predictor consistency require careful integration with the supplied baseline.

related_work.title: PyTorch packed recurrent sequences
contributions: Provides packed execution for variable-length recurrent inputs.
Supports encoding compacted chronological histories without executing padding transitions.
limitations: Packing original left-padded histories using nonzero counts retains incorrect leading positions.
Aligned timestep diagnostics require unpacking and scattering outputs back to their original positions.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces BPR-max to emphasize high-scoring negatives in recurrent recommendation.
Separates ranking probability aggregation from negative-score regularization.
limitations: Does not establish gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.
Competitive negatives can include unobserved relevant items.

related_work.title: MTAM: time-aware attentive recurrent recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for incorporating temporal information into recurrent recommendation.
Motivates testing how recent behavior interacts with historical memory.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed absolute-event target weighting.
Its broader architecture would add complexity beyond the selected early-stage experiment.
